content: Colombia’s central bank is scrutinizing the peso’s surge to determine whether the rally reflects solid fundamentals or speculative inflows, one of its newest board members said in an interview.

title: Italy’s Giorgetti Is Worrying About Fallout From the Trade War
content: Italian Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said he’s concerned about potential damage to European economies from trade tensions and the weakening of the US dollar.

title: Fiscal Discipline Faces Another Downgrade in Japan’s Election
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at the economic policy implications of Sunday’s election in Japan. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: G-7 Vows to Crack Down on China’s Economic Sway, Klingbeil Says
content: The Group of Seven has agreed to ramp up collective efforts to counter China flooding the global markets with its overcapacities, mounting concerns over critical supply chain vulnerabilities and Beijing’s grip on rare earth minerals, according to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil.

title: ECB Seen Opting for Lending Tools Over QE in Future Crises
content: The European Central Bank will pick lending to banks over bond-buying in almost all future situations that require unconventional responses, according to a Bloomberg poll of economists.

title: EU Agrees to Start Talks With Gulf Nations on Strategic Ties
content: European Union member states approved the launch of negotiations with six Gulf countries as the bloc seeks to broaden its international partnerships amid tariff threats from President Donald Trump.

title: Challenges to Fed Independence Resonate Beyond US, Nagel Says
content: Interference in the independence of the Federal Reserve would be felt outside of the US, according to Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel.

title: EU Budget Proposal ‘Dead on Arrival,’ Says Dutch Minister
content: Dutch Finance Minister Eelco Heinen rejected the European Commission’s €2 trillion ($2.3 trillion) budget proposal, calling it “dead on arrival.”

title: Thai Finance Chief Sees US Cutting 36% Tariff on Fresh Proposal
content: Thailand expects the US to reduce a threatened tariff on its exports from 36% to a level in line with regional neighbors after presenting a “very substantial improvement” in a fresh round of talks, Finance Minister Pichai Chunhavajira said.

title: Malaysian Growth Unexpectedly Quickens Despite Trade Risks
content: Malaysia’s economy grew faster than expected in the second quarter, driven by the services sector, even as the country contends with US President Donald Trump’s rollout of global tariffs.

title: Japan Official Urges China to Expand Foreign Investment Quota
content: A Japanese government official called on China to expand a program allowing certain mainland investors to put more money abroad, citing “strong enthusiasm” for Japanese stocks.

title: Sarepta Refused FDA’s Request to Halt Elevidys Shipments
content: Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. has refused to pause all shipments of its Elevidys treatment after three deaths were linked to the company’s gene therapies, the Food and Drug Administration said Friday.

title: Froot Loops, Apple Jacks to Cut Synthetic Dyes by 2027
content: WK Kellogg Co. will remove synthetic dyes from its cereals, including Froot Loops and Apple Jacks, by the end of 2027, joining a growing cohort of other US companies that have committed to eliminate colorants such as Red 40 and Yellow 5 from their foods.

title: Air India Crash Reporting Is ‘Premature,’ NTSB’s Homendy Says
content: Investigators, led by India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau with the assistance of the NTSB, have been piecing together evidence to determine what caused Air India Flight 171 to crash on June 12, killing 260 people.

title: BASF Set to Take Next-Round Bids for Coatings Arm in August
content: BASF SE has asked bidders for its coatings business to submit offers next month after shortlisting suitors for the unit that could be worth €6 billion ($7 billion) or more in a deal, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Otsuka, Lundbeck’s PTSD Drug Fails to Win US FDA Panel Support
content: Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co.’s medicine for post-traumatic stress disorder with partner H. Lundbeck A/S failed to win the backing of US regulatory advisers, a major setback in the drugmakers’ bid to bring the first new drug for the condition to market in more than two decades.

title: Writers Guild Seeks NY Probe of Colbert Show’s Cancellation
content: The Writers Guild of America asked New York Attorney General Letitia James to investigate CBS’s decision to cancel The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, saying the network’s parent company may have given in to political pressure.

title: JFK Lifts Ground Stop Caused by Disabled Aircraft on Runway
content: New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport has lifted a temporary ground stop put in place due to a disabled aircraft on the runway.

title: Chevron CEO Says Hess Outcome Softens Risk for Other Oil Deals
content: Chevron Corp. says the closing of its $53 billion agreement to buy Hess Corp. will ease uncertainty for other deals in the oil industry.

title: Chevron CEO’s Career-Defining Win Means Healing Rift With Exxon
content: As the dust settles from a bruising legal battle over the world’s marquee oil bonanza, the leaders of Exxon Mobil Corp. and Chevron Corp. face a new challenge: collaboration.

title: Iraq Set for Key Oil Cargo Surge in Sign of Increased Output
content: Iraq will raise shipments of a key crude grade next month, part of an enlarged export program indicating that the OPEC+ nation is boosting its oil production.

title: Humana Falls After Losing Bid to Reverse Medicare Bonus Cuts
content: Humana Inc. shares fell after it lost a lawsuit seeking to reverse cuts to its Medicare bonus payments, a blow for the insurer that had hoped the court would restore billions in revenue.

title: Chevron Triumphs Over Exxon, Wins 20-Month Battle to Buy Hess
content: Chevron Corp. has prevailed in a 20-month fight to buy Hess Corp. for $53 billion, overcoming a challenge by arch rival Exxon Mobil Corp. that was unprecedented in the modern history of Big Oil.

title: FDA Is Investigating If Sarepta’s Gene Therapy Should Stay on Market
content: US Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Marty Makary said he’s “taking a hard look” at whether a gene therapy from Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. should remain on the market.

title: Ally Shares Fall as Outlook Disappoints Some Investors
content: Ally Financial Inc. shares fell after the lender left most of its forecast unchanged despite strong second-quarter consumer auto-loan originations and earnings.

title: HSBC Sells French Loan Portfolio to Its Former France Subsidiary
content: HSBC Holdings Plc has sold €6.7 billion ($7.8 billion) of French loans to a consortium that includes its former French subsidiary CCF.

title: Avidbank Files for IPO Ahead of Balance Sheet Restructuring
content: Avidbank Holdings filed for an initial public offering, earmarking a substantial portion of the proceeds help fund a balance sheet restructuring and secure its financial cushion.

title: WNBA’s Caitlin Clark Effect Is Now the Ripple Effect
content: Welcome to Business of Sports, where this week we take a deep dive into the WNBA without Caitlin Clark and the fight with its own players. We also look at what’s going on with Apollo’s push into sports (check out our scoop here), and we interview Valérie Tétreault, director of Montreal’s National Bank Open and only woman to run a top pro tennis tournament, about the loneliness of the long distance tennis player.

title: Grubhub Owner Wonder Seeks Up to $500 Million to Refinance Debt
content: Grubhub Holdings Inc.’s owner Wonder has approached lenders including private credit firms as it seeks to raise between $400 million and $500 million to refinance the food delivery company’s existing debt, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Kraft Heinz’s $4.3 Billion Pension Gives Company Leverage as It Weighs Options
content: Hidden among Kraft Heinz Co.’s brightly colored assets exists an unusual source of value: an over-funded pension plan.

title: Swedish Industry’s Tariff Navigation Clouded by Currency Hit
content: Currency headwinds are darkening the outlook of Sweden’s industrial companies, clouding a fairly resilient performance in the face of US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Garuda New 737 Jet’s Higher Rent May Strain Finances Further
content: Garuda is paying twice as much to lease its latest Boeing Co. 737 Max jet than it does for the older 737 planes in its fleet, another potential blow to its finances as it tries to return to profitability.

title: Netflix Tops Wall Street’s Lofty Estimates, Raises Forecast
content: Netflix Inc. beat expectations for second-quarter results and continues to trounce rival media companies, yet the shares slipped on Friday as investors took a pause after the stock has nearly doubled over the past year.

title: Talen Jumps to Record After Buying Prime Power Plants to Feed AI
content: Talen Energy Corp. shares surged the most ever in intraday trading after announcing a $3.8 billion deal to buy two of the most efficient power plants on the largest US grid, joining a wave of deals by independent generators snapping up gas units to feed AI’s surging demand.

title: Schwab Rises as Earnings Beat on Client Assets, Trading
content: Charles Schwab Corp. rose after the company reported second-quarter earnings that topped estimates as client assets hit a new record and trading revenue increased.

title: Amex Expenses Grow Amid Investments to Keep Customers Spending
content: American Express Co.’s expenses grew in the second quarter as the firm made risk-management and technology investments for its affluent consumers, who continued to spend amid economic uncertainty.
